meaning: To be emotionally overwhelmed or deeply moved — your psychological defenses get 'broken through'. Used for anything from being touched to tears to being provoked/triggered.
meaning_zh: 指心理防线被击穿、情绪失控或深受触动——可以是被感动到哭，也可以是被激怒。
example: 看到那条新闻我直接破防了。
example_pinyin: Kàndào nà tiáo xīnwén wǒ zhíjiē pòfáng le.
example_translation: Seeing that piece of news completely broke me.
context: Originally a gaming term (an enemy's defense being penetrated). Netizens repurposed it for emotional 'defenses', and it exploded across Weibo and Bilibili as the go-to way to say something hit you hard.

meaning: To 'lie flat' — to opt out of relentless striving, reject social pressure to overwork, and settle for a minimal, low-stress life.
meaning_zh: 指放弃拼命奋斗、不再迎合社会压力，选择低欲望、低压力的生活方式。
example: 卷不动了，我选择躺平。
example_pinyin: Juǎn bù dòng le, wǒ xuǎnzé tǎngpíng.
example_translation: I can't keep grinding — I choose to lie flat.
context: A landmark 2021 movement among young Chinese pushing back against '996' overwork culture. Became a cultural lightning rod, even drawing state media commentary. Pairs directly with 内卷.

meaning: 'Involution' — pointless, escalating internal competition where everyone works harder and harder for the same or shrinking rewards.
meaning_zh: 指无意义的过度竞争：大家越来越拼命，回报却没有增加，甚至更少。
example: 这个行业太内卷了，加班到半夜也没用。
example_pinyin: Zhège hángyè tài nèijuǎn le, jiābān dào bànyè yě méi yòng.
example_translation: This industry is so involuted — working till midnight doesn't even help.
context: Borrowed from anthropology ('involution'), it went viral among students and white-collar workers to describe zero-sum rat-race competition. The verb form 卷 (juǎn) alone now means 'to compete obsessively'.

meaning: To feel down, melancholy, or in your feelings. Used as a verb: 我emo了 = 'I'm feeling low.'
meaning_zh: 借自英文，指情绪低落、伤感、陷入负面情绪。“我emo了”就是“我心情很低落”。
example: 半夜听这首歌我又emo了。
example_pinyin: Bànyè tīng zhè shǒu gē wǒ yòu emo le.
example_translation: Listening to this song at midnight made me emo again.
context: Borrowed from the English 'emo' subculture but stripped to just mean 'sad/moody'. Peak usage is the late-night '网抑云' (a pun on NetEase Music) phenomenon of posting melancholy comments after dark.

meaning: An attention-grabbing show-off — someone (or even an animal/object) that's hilariously extra and can't help standing out. Usually affectionate.
meaning_zh: 指特别爱出风头、搞笑又抢眼的人（有时也指动物或物品），多为亲昵的调侃。
example: 我们班的显眼包又在讲笑话了。
example_pinyin: Wǒmen bān de xiǎnyǎnbāo yòu zài jiǎng xiàohuà le.
example_translation: The class clown is telling jokes again.
context: A regional dialect word that went nationwide in 2023 via short-video platforms. Spawned endless '显眼包' compilation videos of goofy pets, kids, and coworkers.

meaning: 'Is it urban/cool/modern or not?' A playful way to ask if something feels stylish, exciting, or big-city. Often just means 'fun/exciting'.
meaning_zh: 用“是不是”的句式问某样东西“洋气不洋气、刺激不刺激”，常表示“好玩、时髦”。
example: 来上海玩，你说city不city？
example_pinyin: Lái Shànghǎi wán, nǐ shuō city bù city?
example_translation: Come hang out in Shanghai — pretty 'city', right?
context: Coined by an American travel vlogger ('保保熊') touring China in 2024. His half-English catchphrase went massively viral, and 'city' became an adjective for cosmopolitan/exciting. A rare English loanword used in a Chinese grammar pattern.

meaning: 'So what?' / 'And then what?' A breezy, unbothered comeback that shrugs off criticism or pressure. An attitude of cheerful defiance.
meaning_zh: “那又怎样？”一种满不在乎、轻松反击的态度，不把别人的评价放在心上。
example: 别人说我躺平，那咋了？我开心就行。
example_pinyin: Biérén shuō wǒ tǎngpíng, nà zǎ le? Wǒ kāixīn jiù xíng.
example_translation: People say I'm slacking off — so what? As long as I'm happy.
context: A Northeastern-dialect flavored phrase that became the anthem of the '那咋了文学' (so-what literature) trend in 2024 — a relaxed, thick-skinned mindset of not letting others' judgments get to you.

meaning: A sense of ease and unbothered calm — being relaxed, composed, and not uptight, even when things go sideways.
meaning_zh: 指从容淡定、不紧绷的状态，即使出了状况也能保持轻松自在。
example: 她面对镜头特别有松弛感。
example_pinyin: Tā miànduì jìngtóu tèbié yǒu sōngchígǎn.
example_translation: She's so at ease in front of the camera.
context: Went viral from a 2022 post about a family staying calm after a travel mishap. Became an aspirational aesthetic on 小红书 (RED) — the coveted, effortless 'relaxed vibe' in fashion, lifestyle, and attitude.

meaning: Amazing! / Incredible! An over-the-top exclamation of praise (occasionally used sarcastically for something amazingly bad).
meaning_zh: “太绝了！”极度夸张的赞叹（偶尔也反讽某样东西烂得离谱）。
example: 这个妆容绝绝子！
example_pinyin: Zhège zhuāngróng juéjuézi!
example_translation: This makeup look is absolutely stunning!
context: Popularized by talent-show fan culture and 小红书 reviewers. The '子' suffix and reduplication give it a cutesy, exaggerated tone — a hallmark of a whole family of '-子' internet words.

meaning: Self-inflicted mental exhaustion — burning yourself out through overthinking, self-doubt, and rumination, rather than from any outside pressure.
meaning_zh: 指因过度思虑、自我怀疑而造成的自我消耗和心累，与外部压力无关。
example: 别再内耗了，事情没那么糟。
example_pinyin: Bié zài nèihào le, shìqíng méi nàme zāo.
example_translation: Stop tormenting yourself over it — things really aren't that bad.
context: The inward twin of 内卷: where 内卷 is exhausting external competition, 内耗 is the exhausting war inside your own head. A dominant term in 2026 mental-health discourse on 小红书 and Weibo, and named an official word of the year.

meaning: The worn-out 'office aura' a job stamps on you — tired eyes, dull clothes, no spark. '一身班味' = reeking of the 9-to-5 grind.
meaning_zh: 指工作在人身上留下的疲惫、暗淡的气息——没精神、没光彩。“一身班味”就是被上班磨得没了朝气。
example: 刚工作半年，我浑身都是班味了。
example_pinyin: Gāng gōngzuò bànnián, wǒ húnshēn dōu shì bānwèi le.
example_translation: Only half a year into the job and I already reek of the office grind.
context: Blew up as young workers joked about losing their pre-job glow. The flip side is '洗掉班味' (washing off the work-smell) — shedding that worn-down look on weekends and holidays. A wry cousin of 躺平 and 内卷.

meaning: The quality of coming across as a real, spontaneous human online — warm and genuine rather than a polished, robotic, over-curated persona. High praise.
meaning_zh: 指在网上显得真实、鲜活、有人情味，而不是精致、刻板、过度包装的人设。
example: 这个博主很有活人感，不像在营业。
example_pinyin: Zhège bózhǔ hěn yǒu huórén gǎn, bù xiàng zài yíngyè.
example_translation: This blogger feels genuinely human — not like they're just 'on the clock.'
context: A 2026 buzzword pushing back against over-produced influencer and celebrity content. Its opposite is 营业 (yíngyè, lit. 'doing business') — performing a role for the camera. To have 活人感 is to feel refreshingly real.

meaning: 'Emotional value' — the comfort, reassurance, and good feelings a person gives you. '提供情绪价值' = to make someone feel good and supported.
meaning_zh: 指一个人能给你带来的安慰、支持和好心情。“提供情绪价值”就是让对方感到被关心、心情变好。
example: 他很会提供情绪价值，跟他聊天很治愈。
example_pinyin: Tā hěn huì tígōng qíngxù jiàzhí, gēn tā liáotiān hěn zhìyù.
example_translation: He's really good at giving emotional support — chatting with him is so healing.
context: Migrated from psychology and relationship advice into everyday dating and consumer talk. By 2026 it's a core yardstick young people use to judge partners, friendships, and even brands and fandoms.

meaning: A loss may turn out to be a blessing in disguise — you can't always tell good fortune from bad. Full form: 塞翁失马，焉知非福.
meaning_zh: 比喻一时的损失也许反而是好事，福祸难料。完整说法：“塞翁失马，焉知非福”。
example: 丢了这份工作也许是塞翁失马，说不定有更好的机会。
example_pinyin: Diūle zhè fèn gōngzuò yěxǔ shì sài wēng shī mǎ, shuōbudìng yǒu gèng hǎo de jīhuì.
example_translation: Losing this job might be a blessing in disguise — maybe a better chance is on the way.
context: A classic chengyu from the Huainanzi: an old man's horse runs off (a loss), then returns with another horse (a gain), which leads to his son breaking a leg (bad), which then spares him from being drafted into war (good). Netizens still drop it in comment sections to console someone after a setback.

meaning: To slack off — goof around, look busy, or quietly do nothing while on the clock, whether at work or in a group task.
meaning_zh: 指偷懒：上班或做事时表面忙碌，实则不干正事、划水。
example: 老板不在，大家都在摸鱼。
example_pinyin: Lǎobǎn bù zài, dàjiā dōu zài mō yú.
example_translation: The boss is out, so everyone's slacking off.
context: From the idiom 浑水摸鱼 ('fishing in muddy waters'). Now the go-to word for skiving at work — a whole 摸鱼 culture of memes, payday-countdown apps, and strategic toilet breaks has grown around it.

meaning: 'Social death' — a moment of public embarrassment so excruciating you wish the ground would swallow you. Short for 社会性死亡.
meaning_zh: “社会性死亡”的简称，指在公众面前极度尴尬、恨不得钻进地缝的时刻。
example: 我叫错了老师的名字，当场社死。
example_pinyin: Wǒ jiào cuò le lǎoshī de míngzì, dāngchǎng shè sǐ.
example_translation: I called the teacher by the wrong name and died of embarrassment on the spot.
context: Full form 社会性死亡. Fuels endless '社死现场' (social-death moment) threads on Weibo and RED where people swap their most cringeworthy public humiliations. Its opposite is 社牛, a fearless social butterfly.

meaning: 'Special-forces tourism' — cramming in as many sights as possible on a lightning, bare-bones trip with minimal sleep and money. Maximum sightseeing, minimum rest.
meaning_zh: 指用最少的时间和金钱、几乎不休息地打卡尽可能多的景点的极限旅行方式。
example: 周末我们特种兵旅游，两天逛了五个城市。
example_pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen tèzhǒngbīng lǚyóu, liǎng tiān guàng le wǔ ge chéngshì.
example_translation: We did special-forces tourism this weekend — five cities in two days.
context: A craze among cash-strapped students: overnight trains, dawn starts, ticking off landmarks military-style. Named an official top-ten phrase and still the label for any punishing whirlwind trip.

meaning: A 'mouth substitute' — someone who says out loud exactly what you were thinking but couldn't put into words. Your spokesperson.
meaning_zh: “嘴巴的替身”，指替你说出你想说却说不出来的话的人。
example: 这个博主简直是我的嘴替，说出了我的心声。
example_pinyin: Zhège bózhǔ jiǎnzhí shì wǒ de zuǐtì, shuō chū le wǒ de xīnshēng.
example_translation: This blogger is totally my mouthpiece — they said exactly what I felt.
context: High praise for a commentator or netizen who nails a shared feeling perfectly. '互联网嘴替' (the internet's mouthpiece) is a badge of honor for anyone who voices what everyone's thinking.

meaning: 'And what can you even do about it?' A deliberately clumsy, sing-song shrug of resignation at life's little annoyances — you can't change it, so why stress.
meaning_zh: “那又能怎么办呢？”一种故意语法不通、无奈又认命的调侃，用来面对生活中的各种烦心事。
example: 周一又来了，如何呢又能怎。
example_pinyin: Zhōuyī yòu lái le, rúhé ne yòu néng zěn.
example_translation: Monday's here again… and what can you even do about it.
context: Grew from singer 单依纯's improvised, grammar-mangling reinterpretation of lyrics on stage, which netizens seized on. An official 2025 top-ten phrase, now tacked onto any complaint — Mondays, plan changes, bad luck — as a comically defeated sigh.

meaning: To feed on illusions — to comfort yourself, or fob others off, with empty, unfulfillable promises.
meaning_zh: 比喻用无法兑现的空想或空头承诺来自我安慰或搪塞别人。网络上常简称“画饼”。
example: 老板又在给我们画饼充饥，说年底一定加薪。
example_pinyin: Lǎobǎn yòu zài gěi wǒmen huà bǐng chōng jī, shuō niándǐ yídìng jiāxīn.
example_translation: The boss is dangling empty promises again, saying we'll definitely get a raise at year-end.
context: A classic chengyu (from the Three Kingdoms era) that thrives online as the clipped verb 画饼 (huàbǐng) — now the standard word for a boss serving up grand, hollow promises to keep you working. A 成语 living a second life as office slang.

meaning: An 'unorthodox hack' — a wildly unconventional, even absurd-looking shortcut that actually works. Applied to anything from cooking to fitness to studying.
meaning_zh: 指看似离谱、不按常理出牌，但实际上很管用的非常规方法或技巧，涵盖做饭、健身、学习等各种生活领域。
example: 用蜜雪冰城的柠檬水腌肉，是我摸索出的邪修做饭法。
example_pinyin: Yòng Mìxuě Bīngchéng de níngméngshuǐ yān ròu, shì wǒ mōsuǒ chū de xiéxiū zuòfàn fǎ.
example_translation: Marinating meat in bubble-tea-chain lemonade is my own unorthodox cooking hack.
context: Borrowed from cultivation-fantasy (修仙) novels, where 邪修 are practitioners who reject the orthodox path for faster, riskier power. 小红书 users repurposed it in 2025–2026 for real life: posts like '兴趣邪修' and '邪修做饭' went viral for cutting corners in delightfully weird ways that actually deliver results.

meaning: A cheeky twist on 'love yourself' — addressing yourself like an old, familiar friend ('old self') rather than an abstract ideal, said as a bit of self-encouragement or self-care.
meaning_zh: “爱自己”的俏皮说法，把“自己”称作相识多年的“老己”，像哄老朋友一样安慰、鼓励自己，冲淡了传统自爱口号的说教感。
example: 今天又搞砸了，没事，爱你老己，明天见。
example_pinyin: Jīntiān yòu gǎozá le, méishì, ài nǐ lǎo jǐ, míngtiān jiàn.
example_translation: Messed up again today — it's fine, love you old self, see you tomorrow.
context: Riffs on a League of Legends voice line, '爱你老妈，明天见' ('love you mum, see you tomorrow'), swapping in '老己'. It swept social media from late 2025 into 2026, with many hailing it as the year's kindest meme for reframing self-compassion without the usual self-help cheesiness.

meaning: A 'crispy-skinned office worker' — someone who looks fine but is physically fragile, falling ill or getting hurt from the mildest overexertion, like a chip that shatters at a touch.
meaning_zh: 形容看起来正常，实则身体很脆弱的年轻上班族——熬夜加班、稍微劳累一下就生病或受伤，像薯片一样一碰就碎。

context: Extended from 2023's '脆皮大学生' (students with mysteriously fragile bodies) to the workplace. Part of the self-mocking 打工人 meme lineage — young workers joking about burnout by comparing themselves to a snack that crumbles under the slightest pressure.

meaning: An ironic caption meaning the opposite of what it says — 'my mental state is great' — used when things are visibly falling apart, as a self-deprecating badge of chaos.
meaning_zh: 字面是“心理状态很好”，实际是反讽——用来自嘲自己其实状态很不稳定、很崩溃，常配在搞怪或狼狈的照片下。
example: 论文还没写完，配图却写着“精神状态良好”。

example_translation: The essay's still unfinished, but the caption says 'mental state: great.'
context: Traces back to '很有精神' ('full of spirit'), a line from a 1969 Japanese war film that became an ironic meme in Chinese gaming and anime circles. By the 2020s it evolved into '精神状态良好' as a deadpan caption netizens slap on photos of their own chaos or mishaps.

meaning: "Here's a toast to yourself" — a self-directed toast used to quietly celebrate your own effort or comfort yourself after a hard day, with no one else's approval required.
meaning_zh: 意思是自己给自己敬一杯酒，用来肯定自己的努力、安慰疲惫的自己，不需要别人的认可，是当代年轻人自我和解、自我鼓励的一种温柔表达。
example: 项目终于交了，先敬自己一杯。
example_pinyin: Xiàngmù zhōngyú jiāo le, xiān jìng zìjǐ yī bēi.
example_translation: The project's finally done — cheers to myself first.

meaning: "I demand a card check!" — a mock-outraged catchphrase shouted when something seems rigged, too good to be true, or suspiciously unfair, whether in a game, a shady purchase, or an absurd real-life coincidence.
meaning_zh: 字面意思是要求检查牌局是否作弊，现在被网友用来调侃任何看起来“太离谱”“太巧”“像开挂”的事情，比如抽卡出货、买到假货、比赛结果离谱等，带着夸张、搞笑的质疑语气。
example: 这个签到奖池居然连续三次抽到隐藏款，我要验牌！
example_pinyin: Zhège qiāndào jiǎngchí jūrán liánxù sān cì chōu dào yǐncáng kuǎn, wǒ yào yàn pái!
example_translation: The check-in prize pool gave me the hidden item three times in a row — I demand a card check!
context: The line comes from a French gambler character's exaggerated, badly-accented Mandarin in the 1990 Stephen Chow film 'God of Gamblers II'. It resurfaced in early 2025 when players noticed an impossible run of matching cards in a game of Sanguosha (Three Kingdoms Kill), and someone spliced the old movie clip over the footage as a joke. It exploded into a catch-all meme for calling out anything absurdly convenient, racking up billions of views and even trending during the 2026 Lunar New Year TV gala.

meaning: A pouty-faced horse plush toy — and by extension, a stand-in for 'I'm having a rough day but I'm allowed to show it,' used self-deprecatingly instead of performing constant positivity.
meaning_zh: 原指义乌工厂在缝制马年吉祥物玩偶时，误把上扬的嘴角缝成了向下撇的“委屈脸”，本该是次品，却因为这副又可怜又可爱的表情意外走红。现在网友用“哭哭马”自嘲情绪低落、诸事不顺，或表达“允许自己不开心”的态度。
example: 今天又被老板骂了，我现在就是一只哭哭马。
example_pinyin: Jīntiān yòu bèi lǎobǎn mà le, wǒ xiànzài jiùshì yī zhī kūkūmǎ.
example_translation: Got yelled at by my boss again today — I'm basically a kūkūmǎ right now.
context: A factory-defect plush toy from Yiwu made ahead of the 2026 Year of the Horse: a stitching mistake gave it a downturned, sulky mouth instead of the standard cheerful smile. Photos of the 'defective' toy went viral because its grumpy little face felt more honest than the usual forced-cheerful mascots, and it became shorthand for rejecting mandatory positivity at work — you're allowed to look like you're having a bad day.

meaning: A sense of personal boundaries — knowing where 'your business' ends and 'someone else's business' begins, and respecting that line in relationships, at work, and online.
meaning_zh: 指人与人交往中对界限的判定和重视程度，强调“你的事归你，我的事归我”，是一种保护个人隐私、情绪和舒适圈，同时也尊重他人空间的相处智慧。
example: 别老问我工资多少，能不能有点边界感？
example_pinyin: Bié lǎo wèn wǒ gōngzī duōshǎo, néng bù néng yǒu diǎn biānjiè gǎn?
example_translation: Stop asking how much I earn — could you have some boundaries?
context: Named in Chinese social platforms' 2026 roundups of the year's defining terms (including 小红书's annual hot-words report), '边界感' tracks a broader shift toward asserting personal space against nosy relatives, oversharing coworkers, and boundary-crossing partners. It's commonly paired with related terms like '活人感' (feeling like a real, un-curated person) as part of a wave of vocabulary about protecting one's inner life from social pressure.

meaning: Using someone's own public online trail — old posts, livestream clips, comments — to check whether their words and actions actually line up, exposing hypocrisy or double standards. Also used for Chinese and international netizens comparing everyday-life details (wages, rent, work hours) across borders.
meaning_zh: 网友利用他人在网络上留下的公开记录（如动态、聊天记录、视频片段）来核实其言行是否一致，戳穿"双标"或言行不一；也指中外网民互相比较工资、物价、工时等日常生活细节，像对两本账一样核实彼此的生活。
example: 他去年说绝不加班，今天被网友"赛博对账"，翻出他加班的动态。
example_pinyin: Tā qùnián shuō juébù jiābān, jīntiān bèi wǎngyǒu "sàibó duìzhàng", fānchū tā jiābān de dòngtài.
example_translation: Last year he swore he'd never work overtime; today netizens "cyber-reconciled" him by digging up his old post about working late.
context: Coined after the 2025 US TikTok ban scare sent American users flooding onto Xiaohongshu (RedNote), where they and Chinese users started comparing rent, wages and daily life like two ledgers being checked against each other (对账 is literally what accountants do). It quickly gained a sharper second use: scrolling someone's own post history to catch them contradicting themselves. Named one of China's official top-10 buzzwords of 2025.

meaning: The deliberate opposite of 内卷 (nèijuǎn, ruinous internal competition for a shrinking pie): instead of fighting harder over the same limited resources, expanding outward for new markets and opportunities — or simply agreeing with rivals to stop the internal rat race together.
meaning_zh: "内卷"的反义词，指不再和身边的人争夺有限的存量资源，而是向外开拓新市场、新资源，或者干脆和大家说好一起停止内部消耗式竞争。
example: 与其卷价格，不如想想怎么外卷，开拓海外市场。
example_pinyin: Yǔqí juǎn jiàgé, bùrú xiǎngxiang zěnme wàijuǎn, kāituò hǎiwài shìchǎng.
example_translation: Instead of racing each other to the bottom on price, why not go external and open up overseas markets instead.
context: Built as a direct mirror of 内卷 — swap 内 (inward) for 外 (outward), keep the "rolling/curling" image. It surfaced heavily in 2026 commentary on Chinese carmakers and manufacturers stuck in brutal price wars, with people urging firms to "外卷" — grow the whole pie abroad — instead of "内卷" against each other at home.

meaning: A joking "toll" — a cat photo — that new foreign users on Xiaohongshu (RedNote) are told they must "pay" before being welcomed in; posting a pet pic as a friendly icebreaker when introducing yourself on the platform.
meaning_zh: 外国新用户在小红书上自我介绍时，被中国网友开玩笑要求先晒一张自家猫的照片作为"入场费"，戏称为"交猫税"，后来也扩展到晒狗、马、羊等各种宠物。
example: 刚注册小红书就有人让我先交猫税，我赶紧发了张我家猫主子的照片。
example_pinyin: Gāng zhùcè Xiǎohóngshū jiù yǒu rén ràng wǒ xiān jiāo māoshuì, wǒ gǎnjǐn fāle zhāng wǒjiā māo zhǔzi de zhàopiàn.
example_translation: I'd barely signed up for RedNote before someone told me to pay the cat tax, so I quickly posted a photo of my cat.
context: Went viral in January 2025 when the looming US TikTok ban sent American "TikTok refugees" flooding onto Xiaohongshu. Chinese users welcomed them by jokingly demanding a "cat tax" — a cute pet photo — before letting them settle in, turning it into a good-natured cross-cultural icebreaker that's still referenced whenever new foreign users show up.

meaning: "There's no 300 taels of silver buried here" — said of someone whose clumsy denial or cover-up ends up proving exactly the thing they were trying to hide; the harder they protest, the more obviously guilty they look.
meaning_zh: 比喻想要隐瞒、掩盖真相的人，因为手法笨拙，反而弄巧成拙，暴露了自己想掩盖的事实；越是极力否认，越显得心虚。

example_translation: He kept insisting "I really didn't peek at her phone" — which basically proved that he did.
context: From an old folk tale: a man buried silver, then worried people would suspect him, so he planted a sign reading "there's no 300 taels of silver buried here." meaning: The ultimate deadpan non-answer. Reply '不知道，我的身材很曼妙' ('no idea — my figure is graceful') to any question you'd rather dodge: an absurd swerve plus shameless self-praise. Swap in other words (我的睡眠很曼妙…) to fit the situation.
meaning_zh: 万能的答非所问回复公式：别人问什么都回一句"不知道，我的身材很曼妙"，用荒诞的自夸化解一切严肃提问，是"已读乱回"的天花板。
example: 老板问我方案写完了吗？不知道，我的身材很曼妙。

example_translation: The boss asked if I'd finished the proposal? No idea — my figure is graceful.
context: Born in an April 2025 Taobao dress review: a shopper asked 'does this dress make hips look wide?' and another buyer replied 'no idea, my figure is graceful'. The gloriously useless answer simmered in fashion circles until January 2026, when actress Yang Mi's studio used it and it exploded into the meme of the new year, spawning endless 曼妙 variants.

meaning: Deliberately answering a message with cheerful nonsense — you've read it, you just refuse to engage seriously. A playful dodge that deflates awkward or nosy questions with absurdity rather than silence.
meaning_zh: 看了消息却故意胡乱回复，答非所问。用无厘头的回答把严肃或尴尬的话题解构掉，是比"已读不回"更有喜感的社交智慧。

meaning: Pre-fabricated WeChat Moments: batch-shooting and editing photos during a trip or event, saving the location tag, then drip-feeding the posts over later days or weeks as if they were live. Life run like a content production line.
meaning_zh: 提前拍好、修好、配好文案的朋友圈素材，之后再分批"新鲜"发布。像预制菜一样，把生活的记录变成一条内容生产线。

Went viral in September 2024 as netizens admitted to stockpiling polished holiday photos and scheduling them out, and it still circulates in 2026 alongside spin-offs like 预制人生 ('pre-made life'). meaning: Running on autopilot: body present, soul offline. Describes the numb, NPC-like state of grinding through work and chores with zero emotional response — alive on paper, faintly dead inside.
meaning_zh: 形容表面正常运转、内心却麻木空虚的状态：机械地上班干活，毫无情绪波动，像个NPC——人还活着，心已下线。

meaning: The counterpart to the already-viral 内耗 (grinding yourself down with internal anxiety): instead of stewing on stress privately, you channel it outward, into action or onto other people. Used both as a genuine coping tip and as a wry admission of taking frustration out on others.
meaning_zh: 与"内耗"相对，指不把焦虑和负面情绪压在心里自我消耗，而是转向外部——投入实际行动，或者发泄给别人。既可以是积极意义上的"把精力用在做事上"，也可以带点自嘲或吐槽的意味。

example_translation: Instead of stewing over it internally, might as well channel it outward — just go rewrite the proposal.

meaning: Treats real life as if it's a live-service video game you're stuck grinding: birth is "registering an account," your ID number is your "UID," commuting is a "daily quest," and a bad day is the server "acting up" or under "maintenance." A humorous lens for turning mundane hardship into something you can shrug off like a game glitch.
meaning_zh: 把现实生活比喻成一款正在运营的网络游戏：出生是"注册账号"，身份证号是"UID"，上班通勤是"每日任务"，倒霉的一天就是"服务器又抽风/维护了"。用游戏化的调侃口吻消解现实压力。
example: 别问了，地球online今天又在维护，什么事都不顺。
example_pinyin: Bié wèn le, dìqiú online jīntiān yòu zài wéihù, shénme shì dōu bù shùn.
example_translation: Don't even ask — Earth Online is under maintenance again today, nothing's going right.
context: A long-running internet framing (netizens trace casual use back well over a decade) that resurged hard in 2026 as young people leaned harder into gaming vocabulary to describe burnout: work is "grinding," exams are "story quests," and a rough patch is just bad server luck — never your fault, and never permanent.

sources.note: 百度百科：地球online（网络流行语）
腾讯新闻：火爆全网！这届年轻人，把生活玩成了"地球online"在线游戏

meaning: A backlash against the heavily filtered, perfectly curated "精致生活" (exquisite lifestyle) aesthetic that dominated lifestyle social media for years. 反精致 content is deliberately unpolished, slightly messy, and shot on the fly — and it's now what actually performs well, because audiences are tired of feeling inadequate next to fake-perfect feeds.
meaning_zh: 对多年来社交媒体上滤镜满满、摆拍精致的"精致生活"审美的一种反弹。"反精致"内容故意不加修饰、随手拍、甚至有点丑，反而因为真实感更受欢迎，因为大家看腻了假完美的生活方式。
example: 现在小红书都流行反精致了，随手拍的丑照反而比精修图火。
example_pinyin: Xiànzài Xiǎohóngshū dōu liúxíng fǎn jīngzhì le, shùnshǒu pāi de chǒu zhào fǎn'ér bǐ jīngxiū tú huǒ.
example_translation: Anti-polish is trending on Xiaohongshu now — casual ugly snapshots actually outperform heavily edited photos.
context: Emerged in 2026 as Xiaohongshu users and bloggers reported aesthetic fatigue with the platform's trademark filtered, staged content. Creators found that rougher, more candid posts got better engagement, and 反精致 became the label for this shift away from curated perfection toward visible imperfection as the new marker of authenticity.

sources.note: 光明网：当代年轻人"反向消费"的典型表现（对"精致穷/假精致"消费的反思）
澎湃新闻：年轻人为什么被"假精致"的生活掏空？

meaning: Shorthand for a very specific parental deflection tactic: instead of engaging with a real problem (career, relationships, emotions), an elder reduces it to a minor physical ailment and prescribes a home remedy — "your liver's overheated, drink some luffa soup." Now used generally to mock anyone who dodges the actual issue with vague, unhelpful concern.
meaning_zh: 指一种典型的家长式回避方式：面对子女真正的问题（工作、感情、情绪），长辈不去正面回应，而是把一切归结为"上火"之类的小毛病，开出"喝点丝瓜汤"这种食疗偏方来打发。现在泛指任何用空洞、不解决问题的"关心"来回避正题的行为。
example: 跟我妈说压力大想辞职，她说是我肝火旺，让我喝丝瓜汤。
example_pinyin: Gēn wǒ mā shuō yālì dà xiǎng cízhí, tā shuō shì wǒ gānhuǒ wàng, ràng wǒ hē sīguā tāng.
example_translation: I told my mum I'm stressed and want to quit, and she said it's just liver heat and told me to drink luffa soup.
context: Went viral in 2025 from short-video creator @累子's family comedy sketches, where an on-screen parent responds to every real problem with the same deflection: "drink some luffa soup for your liver." It stuck because so many viewers recognised the pattern from their own families — turning emotional or structural problems into food-therapy small talk — and it's remained in steady circulation into 2026.

sources.note: 百度百科：丝瓜汤（网络热梗）
光明网：火遍全网的"丝瓜汤"到底是啥？想喝就能喝吗？

pinyin: zuò wán nǐ de, zuò nǐ de
meaning: A catchphrase meaning 'handle what's yours, mind your own business, stay in your lane' — used self-deprecatingly or as a pep talk to project unbothered confidence while everything around you is chaos.
meaning_zh: 意为专注做好自己的事，不受外界干扰，常用来自嘲或打气——在手忙脚乱、事情一堆的情况下依然保持自信从容的状态。
example: 任务再多也别慌，做完你的，做你的。
example_pinyin: Rènwù zài duō yě bié huāng, zuò wán nǐ de, zuò nǐ de.
example_translation: No matter how much is on your plate, don't panic — finish what's yours, do your own thing.
context: From 鸡排哥 (Chicken Cutlet Bro), a street vendor in Jingdezhen who, amid the after-school rush at his stall, calmly told the crowd '做完你的做你的……这种场面，我还是在控制' (finish yours, do yours... I've still got this scene under control) in his thick local accent. His unbothered, self-assured delivery went viral, and netizens now quote the line to self-motivate or self-mock when swamped.

sources.note: 百度百科：做完你的做你的（源自景德镇"鸡排哥"）

meaning: A coffee shop set in a rural/countryside location — part of a lifestyle trend blending slow, pastoral living with the urban ritual of grabbing a coffee. Shorthand for the 'escape the city, briefly' fantasy.
meaning_zh: 指开在乡村里的咖啡馆，是融合田园慢生活与城市咖啡消费习惯的新业态，寄托着都市人对逃离城市、回归田园生活的向往。
example: 周末不想挤景点，就去郊外的村咖坐一下午。
example_pinyin: Zhōumò bù xiǎng jǐ jǐngdiǎn, jiù qù jiāowài de cūn kā zuò yí xiàwǔ.
example_translation: I don't feel like fighting crowds at tourist spots this weekend, so I'm just going to sit at a village coffee shop out in the countryside all afternoon.
context: Took off after villages like Yucun (余村) in Anji County (安吉县), Zhejiang went viral for their scenic countryside cafés, drawing city dwellers for weekend day trips. It made 2025's top-ten internet buzzword list and is still widely used for the broader 'slow life, briefly' aesthetic that blends rural charm with city coffee culture.

sources.note: 百度百科：村咖（乡村咖啡馆）
武汉市农业农村局："村咖"究竟卖的啥

meaning: A fill-in-the-blank template from MBTI/personality-typing culture: after someone does or says something characteristic, netizens jokingly "confirm" them as a certain personality type — "J人" (the planner), "P人" (the improviser), or any invented label. Used to gently roast or affectionately type-cast someone's behaviour.
meaning_zh: 网友根据一个人的言行举止，调侃式地把ta“归类”进某种人格标签的万能句式，如“确认为J人”（计划型人格）、“确认为P人”（随性型人格），也能自创任意标签，用来俏皮地吐槽或“认证”某人的性格特点。
example: 出门前把行程表打印出来还带了备用方案，确认为J人格。
example_pinyin: Chūmén qián bǎ xíngchéngbiǎo dǎyìn chūlái hái dàile bèiyòng fāng'àn, quèrèn wéi J réngé.
example_translation: Printed out the itinerary before leaving and brought a backup plan too — confirmed J personality.
context: 源自MBTI人格测试在国内网络的走红：网友把16型人格里的字母（如判断型的J、知觉型的P）当作性格标签玩梗，“确认为XX人格”成了万能句式，只要谁的行为符合某种刻板印象就会被网友“盖章认证”，衍生出无数自创人格标签用来抖机灵。

sources.note: 扬子晚报："确诊为傻乐者"，SBTI人格测试刷屏朋友圈（MBTI式"确认/确诊为XX人格"梗）
中国江苏网：SBTI全网爆火，你去认领人格标签了么？

meaning: Classic chengyu for being self-contradictory — saying or doing two things that can't both be true. Constantly deployed in comment sections to call out hypocrisy, flip-flopping, or talking out of both sides of one's mouth.
meaning_zh: 出自《韩非子》，讲一个楚国人卖矛又卖盾，夸自己的盾无坚不摧，又夸自己的矛无所不破——两种说法互相冲突。现多用于评论区吐槽某人言行前后不一致、说一套做一套的“双标”行为。
example: 你上一秒说不看重学历，下一秒又嫌弃对方学历低，这不是自相矛盾吗？
example_pinyin: Nǐ shàng yī miǎo shuō bù kànzhòng xuélì, xià yī miǎo yòu xiánqì duìfāng xuélì dī, zhè bùshì zìxiāngmáodùn ma?
example_translation: One second you say you don't care about qualifications, the next you're looking down on someone for having a lower one — isn't that contradicting yourself?
context: 源自《韩非子·难一》里卖矛又卖盾的商人，吹嘘矛无所不破、盾无坚不摧，被人问“以子之矛陷子之盾何如”当场语塞。这个两千多年前的寓言至今仍是评论区吐槽“双标”“说话前后不一”的高频成语，尤其常见于扒名人言论前后矛盾的截图对比帖。

sources.note: 百度百科：自相矛盾（汉语成语）
汉典：自相矛盾的解释、出处（《韩非子·难一》）

meaning: An adverb dropped before a verb to say something happened directly, smoothly, and completely out in the open — "just straight-up ___." Started out describing something fresh, dewy and full of life (bright eyes, crisp vegetables), then got repurposed into the viral sentence template "水灵灵地 + verb."
meaning_zh: 本义形容人或物新鲜、有光泽、有精神（比如眼睛水灵灵的）。网络流行用法中，“水灵灵地”被当作副词放在动词前，强调事情发生得直接、坦荡、毫不遮掩，带点意外或自嘲的意味，例如“水灵灵地被裁员了”。
example: 我水灵灵地就把工资全花光了。
example_pinyin: Wǒ shuǐ línglíng de jiù bǎ gōngzī quán huā guāng le.
example_translation: I just straight-up blew my entire paycheck.
context: 源自2024年韩国女团成员洪恩采接受采访时说的“我在中间显得水灵灵的”，被网友玩梗后延伸出“水灵灵地+动词”的句式，形容一件事发生得毫无征兆、直白坦率。2024年入选《咬文嚼字》年度十大流行语，到2026年仍在社交平台被广泛套用造句。

sources.note: 百度百科：水灵灵（网络流行语）
光明网：“水灵灵地”：叠音表达增添生动感

meaning: To recommend a product so persuasively it plants a craving to buy it in someone (or to catch that craving yourself). The exact counterpart of 拔草 ("pull the grass") — finally buying the thing, or giving up on wanting it. Core vocabulary of Xiaohongshu/RedNote-style recommendation culture.
meaning_zh: 指通过分享、推荐激起别人（或自己）对某样东西的购买欲望，让“想要”的念头像草一样在心里“种”下来。与“拔草”相对——拔草指最终买了（欲望被满足）或打消了购买念头。
example: 这个博主又给我种草了一支新口红。
example_pinyin: Zhège bózhǔ yòu gěi wǒ zhòngcǎo le yì zhī xīn kǒuhóng.
example_translation: That influencer got me hooked on wanting a new lipstick again.
context: 源自美妆论坛时代网友分享好物的说法，随小红书等“种草经济”平台兴起而成为全民热词，是理解当下网络消费文化绕不开的词，如今每次刷到心动好物都会说“被种草了”。

sources.note: 百度百科：种草（网络流行语）
南方网：粤东野语｜“种草”

meaning: Someone who stays even-keeled about everything — barely any emotional highs or lows, answers drama with a flat "算了" (never mind) or "OK," hard to ruffle. The calm counterpart to 浓人.
meaning_zh: 指性格平和、情绪波动小、对事情不太上心的人，遇事常说“算了”“行”“没事”，追求情绪稳定、远离精神内耗，是一种自我调侃式的性格标签。
example: 别指望她会激动，她是标准的淡人。
example_pinyin: Bié zhǐwàng tā huì jīdòng, tā shì biāozhǔn de dànrén.
example_translation: Don't expect her to get worked up — she's a textbook "dàn person."
context: 2024年前后由性格分类梗演变而来，与“浓人”相对，反映年轻人对情绪稳定、佛系生活方式的推崇，2026年仍是小红书等平台常见的自我贴标签方式。

sources.note: 百度百科：淡人和浓人
新华网：“淡人”也可以充满生命力

meaning: The opposite of 淡人 — someone emotionally intense and expressive, quick to share feelings, craves attention and closeness, wears every mood right on their sleeve.
meaning_zh: 指情感丰富、热情外露、喜怒哀乐都写在脸上、渴望被关注和亲近的人，分享欲和倾诉欲都很强，与“淡人”相对。
example: 我是超级浓人，一有开心事就想告诉全世界。
example_pinyin: Wǒ shì chāojí nóngrén, yī yǒu kāixīn shì jiù xiǎng gàosù quán shìjiè.
example_translation: I'm such a "nóng person" — the second something good happens I want to tell the whole world.
context: 与“淡人”配套出现的性格标签梗，用来调侃自己或他人情绪外放、分享欲强的性格类型，常见于小红书等平台的人格分类讨论中。

sources.note: 百度百科：淡人和浓人
澎湃新闻：谁是浓人，谁是淡人？社交标签与无法被定义的自我

meaning: A self-mocking label netizens gave themselves after a celebrity used it as an insult for jealous critics; now used to jokingly claim you're broke, ordinary, or a bit envious — reclaiming the jab as a badge of humour rather than an attack.
meaning_zh: 网友自嘲用语。源自某明星怼网友时把“酸葡萄”说成“酸黄瓜”，本意是讽刺见不得别人好、爱说风凉话的人，后被网友反过来自称，变成一种戏谑的自嘲身份标签，用来调侃自己普通、没钱或有点羡慕别人。
example: 别问我今年攒了多少钱，我就是个酸黄瓜。
example_pinyin: Bié wèn wǒ jīnnián zǎn le duōshǎo qián, wǒ jiùshì gè suān huáng guā.
example_translation: Don't ask me how much I've saved this year — I'm just a "sour cucumber."
context: In January 2026, actress 闫学晶 dismissed online criticism of her lavish spending by calling her critics "酸黄瓜" — a garbled version of the idiom 酸葡萄 ("sour grapes"). The slip of the tongue went viral: rather than taking offence, netizens embraced "酸黄瓜" as a new self-deprecating label, claiming the identity themselves whenever joking about being broke, unremarkable, or quietly envious, turning an insult into shared comic relief.

sources.note: 腾讯新闻：宋晓峰直播遭酸黄瓜刷屏无奈中断
新浪财经：闫学晶“闭麦”，2026年第一个热梗酸到了谁？

meaning: A borrowed philosophy term (via Sartre, Foucault) that's become netizen shorthand for reclaiming personal agency — refusing to live by others' expectations, rejecting people-pleasing, and daring to be disliked in order to live authentically.
meaning_zh: 本是哲学术语（常引用萨特、福柯），在网络语境中指找回自我掌控感：拒绝活成他人期待的样子，摆脱讨好型人格，拥有“被讨厌的勇气”，活出真正的自己。2026年被小红书评为年度十大热词之一。
example: 这件事我想清楚了，我要找回自己的主体性。
example_pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ xiǎng qīngchǔ le, wǒ yào zhǎohuí zìjǐ de zhǔtǐxìng.
example_translation: I've thought it through — I'm reclaiming my own subjectivity.
context: As Chinese social media users grew tired of self-optimisation and people-pleasing, "主体性" spread on 小红书 as a way to talk about resisting social conditioning and other people's judgement. Posts invoking the term often cite Sartre or Foucault, discussing why "the more subjectivity you have, the more enemies you make" — it was named one of Xiaohongshu's top ten hot words of 2026, alongside 活人感 and 边界感, as part of a wider mood of guarding one's inner life.

sources.note: 三联生活周刊：从来没为自己活过的年轻人，决定找回“主体性”
半月谈：“心流时刻”找回主体性

meaning: Tech-world netizen slang for running and maintaining the open-source AI agent OpenClaw, whose bright red lobster-claw logo earned it the nickname "龙虾" (lobster) — 'raising a lobster' means babysitting your AI agent: watching its status, fixing its errors, feeding it new tools.
meaning_zh: 科技圈网络热梗，指使用和维护开源AI智能体OpenClaw。因其鲜红色的龙虾钳子图标，网友昵称它为“龙虾”，“养龙虾”便成了调侃自己在电脑里布置、盯着、维护这个AI智能体运行状态的说法。
example: 别找我，我在家养龙虾呢，得盯着它跑任务。
example_pinyin: Bié zhǎo wǒ, wǒ zài jiā yǎng lóngxiā ne, děi dīngzhe tā pǎo rènwù.
example_translation: Don't bother me, I'm "raising my lobster" at home — gotta watch it run its tasks.
context: OpenClaw, an open-source AI agent tool, went viral in 2026 for its vivid red lobster-claw ("Claw") logo and branding, which plays on the literal meaning of "claw." Developers and hobbyists who set it up and keep it running started calling the process "养龙虾" (raising a lobster) — half in-joke, half accurate description of the fussing, debugging, and monitoring involved in keeping an AI agent working reliably.

meaning: A satirical label for office workers who watch the clock obsessively and bolt the second work hours end, terrified that lingering an extra minute will get them saddled with last-minute tasks. Part of the Year-of-the-Horse (2026) genre of workplace "confirmed diagnosis" memes.
meaning_zh: 指那些死死盯着下班时间、一到点就立刻收拾走人的打工人，生怕多待一秒就被临时安排新工作。是马年（2026）职场“确诊体”系列热梗之一。
example: 一到六点，他就成了卡急马，秒没影。
example_pinyin: Yī dào liù diǎn, tā jiù chéngle kǎjímǎ, miǎo méiyǐng.
example_translation: The second it hits 6pm, he turns into a "kǎjímǎ" — gone in a flash.
context: Emerged on Douyin in January 2026, riding the Year-of-the-Horse wave of workplace horse puns (alongside 脆皮打工人 and 哭哭马, already in the deck). 卡 (clock precisely) + 急 (anxious) + 马 (horse, the zodiac tie-in) captures the dread of being handed extra work right at knock-off time, part of a mock self-diagnosis trend where young workers jokingly "confirm" their own office-induced syndromes.

sources.note: 百度百科《卡急马》

meaning: A euphemistic script for airing a grievance without confrontation: preface a complaint by saying you assumed you were just being oversensitive, then gently insist that, no, it genuinely bothered you. Used to call out anything from a backhanded compliment to a broken workplace promise while staying polite.
meaning_zh: 一种委婉表达不满的话术公式：先说“以为是自己敏感了”，再补一句“但确实不舒服”，以温和克制的方式点出对方的冒犯，而不撕破脸。
example: 当时以为是我敏感了，但确实不舒服。
example_pinyin: Dāngshí yǐwéi shì wǒ mǐngǎn le, dàn quèshí bù shūfu.
example_translation: At the time I thought I was just being sensitive, but I really was uncomfortable.
context: Kicked off when actor 王鹤棣 (Wang Hedi) used this phrasing on a variety show to describe how a past controversy had felt. Netizens turned his sentence into a reusable template, following earlier "X文学" genres like 废话文学 and 发疯文学 (also in the deck), and it quickly spread from celebrity gossip threads into everyday complaints about pushy bosses, awkward dates and thesis defences.

sources.note: 潮新闻《"不舒服文学"刷屏全网：温柔表达背后，是当代年轻人的社交情绪突围》

meaning: A sung, deadpan catchphrase quoted whenever something (or someone) is mildly, comically alarming — dropped into comments and captions as an ironic overreaction, riffing on the original song's flat AI-generated delivery.
meaning_zh: 源自一首AI神曲的经典台词，语气平淡却带着夸张的“被吓到”意味，现在被网友用来吐槽任何有点离谱、意外或惊悚的小事，带有调侃和无奈的反差萌。
example: 你这发型也太抽象了吧，OMG你吓到我了。
example_pinyin: Nǐ zhè fàxíng yě tài chōuxiàng le ba, OMG nǐ xiàdào wǒ le.
example_translation: That haircut is way too out there — OMG, you scared me.
context: From papi酱's July 2026 AI-composed single《生气了》("Angry"), for which she wrote the lyrics while AI handled the composition and vocals. The flat, slightly unsettling AI delivery of "Oh my god你吓到我了" turned the line into an instant meme, spawning duets, remixes and reaction clips across Douyin and Bilibili.

meaning: A metaphor for one's limited mental/emotional energy for socialising, likened to a phone battery: interacting with people drains it, alone time recharges it. Used to self-diagnose why you want to skip plans or need space.
meaning_zh: 把社交精力比作手机电量的说法，社交会“耗电”，独处则用来“充电”。年轻人常用来自嘲式地解释自己为什么想少社交或需要独处。
example: 今天见了三拨人，我的社交电池已经耗光了，晚上谁也不见。
example_pinyin: Jīntiān jiànle sān bō rén, wǒ de shèjiāo diànchí yǐjīng hàoguāng le, wǎnshang shéi yě bú jiàn.
example_translation: I've met three different groups of people today — my social battery is completely drained, I'm not seeing anyone tonight.
context: Borrowed from the English "social battery" concept and popularised on Xiaohongshu/Weibo as a self-diagnostic label. Spawned the related term 社交省电模式 (social power-saving mode) — deliberately cutting back on socialising to protect the last bit of "charge" — letting people decline plans without guilt.

meaning: Formally means "to pay tribute," but as a Bilibili bullet-comment (danmu) it's fired off en masse whenever a video shows courage, kindness, resilience, or everyday heroism — a scrolling wave of sincere, collective respect.
meaning_zh: 本义是“表达敬意”，如今是B站弹幕文化里的高频词——每当视频中出现善良、勇敢、坚韧或英雄主义的画面，网友就会刷“致敬”弹幕，表达最朴素真诚的敬意。
example: 视频里那位截肢后依然乐观生活的博主一出现，满屏都是“致敬”的弹幕。
example_pinyin: Shìpín lǐ nà wèi jiézhī hòu yīrán lèguān shēnghuó de bózhǔ yī chūxiàn, mǎn píng dōu shì “zhìjìng” de dànmù.
example_translation: The moment the blogger who stayed optimistic after losing a limb appeared, the whole screen filled with "zhìjìng" bullet comments.
context: Named Bilibili's 2025 Danmu of the Year, sent over 22.82 million times by more than 4.59 million users (80% Gen Z). Marks a shift in bullet-comment culture away from pure joking toward sincere, collective displays of respect for ordinary people's courage and kindness.

meaning: Not a phrase with a fixed meaning but a whole video-meme genre: short, dramatically-scored clips of real pet cats "acting out" exaggerated storylines via dubbed dialogue and meme music stings. Imported from Japanese internet culture, it exploded across 小红书/B站/抖音 starting early 2026. Two "star" cats anchor the genre — a silver-shaded cat nicknamed 胖虎/Tiger (owned by Bilibili uploader 瘦巴巴的胖虎) and a golden-shaded cat owned by Xiaohongshu user 苍天呐 — plus crossover spin-offs like cats "cosplaying" as anime characters.
meaning_zh: 并非一个有固定含义的词，而是一整套视频meme类型：把家养猫的片段配上夸张的配音和音效剪成“小剧场”。源自日本网络文化，2026年初起在小红书、B站、抖音全网爆火。核心“顶流”猫包括银渐层“胖虎/Tiger”（B站UP主“瘦巴巴的胖虎”家的猫）和金渐层猫（小红书用户“苍天呐”家的猫），还衍生出猫“cos”动漫角色跳舞等玩法。
example: 刷到猫meme的第一反应：这猫怎么比我还会演。
example_pinyin: Shuā dào māo meme de dì yī fǎnyìng: zhè māo zěnme bǐ wǒ hái huì yǎn.
example_translation: My first reaction scrolling past a cat meme clip: how is this cat a better actor than me.
context: Traces back to Japanese cat-owner accounts dubbing dramatic "storylines" over everyday footage of their cats; Chinese creators reposted the clips and then remade the format locally, and by 2026 the #猫meme tag had racked up over 750 million views on Xiaohongshu alone. Its selling point is that the narrative itself is the joke — the cat IS the plot, not just a reaction caption — which is why fan-made variants (cats redubbed as anime characters, crossover "duets" between the two star cats) keep multiplying.

萌娘百科《猫Meme》

meaning: Not an actual tax — a satirical nickname netizens gave to a wave of August 2026 price hikes on the "office-worker three-piece set" (laptop, phone, e-bike), which they blame on AI chip demand eating up manufacturing capacity: a mainstream laptop model jumped from about 4,800rmb in June to 7,899rmb in July, sub-1,000rmb entry-level phones are being discontinued, and e-bike brands have raised prices 200–300rmb since April.
meaning_zh: 并非真实存在的税种，而是网友对2026年8月“打工人三件套”（电脑、手机、电动车）集体涨价的调侃说法，把涨价原因归咎于AI芯片产能被抢占：某笔记本电脑从6月约4800元涨到7月7899元，涨幅超六成；千元入门机加速下架；雅迪、爱玛等电动车品牌4月以来普涨200至300元。
example: 工资没涨，AI税倒是先涨了。
example_pinyin: Gōngzī méi zhǎng, AI shuì dào shì xiān zhǎng le.
example_translation: My salary hasn't gone up, but the "AI tax" sure has.
context: Coined after the Weibo topic "打工人三件套集体大涨价" ("office workers' three-piece set all rising in price together") trended in August 2026, tying together separate price surges — laptops, budget phones, e-bikes — under one sarcastic banner blaming the AI boom's chip and component demand for squeezing ordinary consumers, even though none of the three products run AI hardware themselves.

meaning: ACG (anime/comic/game, also idol fandom) merchandise — badges, acrylic stands, keychains, postcards and the like — that fans collect and trade.
meaning_zh: "谷子"是英语单词"goods"的谐音简称，指二次元（动漫、游戏、偶像）周边商品，比如吧唧（徽章）、亚克力立牌、卡片、挂件等。收藏这些商品的人聚在一起，就形成了所谓的"谷圈"。
example: 她这个月工资全用来买新出的谷子了，光吧唧就买了二十个。
example_pinyin: Tā zhège yuè gōngzī quán yòng lái mǎi xīn chū de gǔzi le, guāng bājī jiù mǎi le èrshí gè.
example_translation: She spent her whole month's salary on the new merch drop — twenty badges alone.
context: "谷子"来自英文"goods"的音译，最早在ACG（动画、漫画、游戏）粉丝圈流行开来，用来统称官方或授权发售的角色周边商品，收藏者聚集形成的社群叫"谷圈"，价位从低到高常被戏称为"普谷""湖景谷""海景谷"。这股风气如今也蔓延到偶像饭圈，"入谷"就是开始收藏某个角色或偶像周边的意思。

meaning: A "jinx": confidently praising or predicting that someone/something will succeed, which — as if cursed — ends up causing the opposite outcome. The reverse of a supportive boost.
meaning_zh: "毒奶"源自电竞圈，"奶"本指给队友加血、看好并夸赞某一方，是祝福的意思；但被夸的一方偏偏在此后犯错或翻车，这种"一夸就崩"的现象就叫"毒奶"，也就是变了质、起反作用的祝福。
example: 解说刚说他这把稳了，转头就送了人头，这波纯纯毒奶。
example_pinyin: Jiěshuō gāng shuō tā zhè bǎ wěn le, zhuǎntóu jiù sòng le réntóu, zhè bō chúnchún dúnǎi.
example_translation: The commentator had just said he had this round locked in, then he immediately fed a kill — a total jinx.
context: "奶"最早是《魔兽世界》等游戏里对治疗/辅助职业的称呼，后引申为"看好、力挺"的意思；解说员夸某选手"稳赢"，对方却立刻失误翻盘，网友便把这种"祝福变诅咒"的效果戏称为"毒奶"。如今也常用于追星、考试、比赛预测等日常场合，比如夸朋友"这次肯定过"，结果对方没过，就会被调侃"你毒奶他了"。

meaning: A satirical phrase for a "heads-I-win-tails-you-lose" con: someone lowballs the quantity or scope of work before it starts, then inflates it afterwards to demand extra payment. Netizens now use it generically for any deal where the other side quietly changes the numbers depending on who owes whom.
meaning_zh: 形容"干活时按小的算、结账时按大的算"的双标讹诈——事前把工作量往少了说，事后又往多了算，反过来找你多要钱。现已成为网友形容类似双标坑人套路的通用说法。
example: 说好4亩地400块，割完非说有5亩多要加钱，这不就是典型的割四赔五。
example_pinyin: Shuō hǎo sì mǔ dì sìbǎi kuài, gēwán fēi shuō yǒu wǔ mǔ duō yào jiā qián, zhè bù jiù shì diǎnxíng de gē sì péi wǔ.
example_translation: They agreed on 4 mu of land for 400rmb, then after the harvest insisted it was actually over 5 mu and demanded more money — classic "harvest four, compensate five."
context: Originated from a May 2026 dispute in Hubei: a young Henan couple who'd taken out a loan to buy a combine harvester travelled to cut wheat for a farmer who first quoted the field at 5 mu, they settled on 4 mu for 400rmb, but after the harvest she claimed it was actually 5.2 mu and refused to pay unless they compensated her for "spilled grain." The story went viral for exposing a common exploitation pattern against migrant harvest workers, and "割四赔五" stuck as the name for that pattern.

meaning: "Traceless recall" — a July 2026 WeChat update (v8.0.76) letting you delete the grey "you recalled a message" notice from your own chat log after recalling a message. The catch: it only clears your side — the other person's screen still shows the recall notice, so nothing is actually hidden from them.
meaning_zh: 微信2026年7月更新的功能：撤回消息后，可以长按删除自己这边"你撤回了一条消息"的灰色提示。但这只对自己有效，对方那边照样能看到撤回提示，并没有真的"消失无痕"。
example: 我把打错的话撤回了，还用无痕撤回删了提示，可对面还是能看到"对方撤回了一条消息"，一点用都没有。
example_pinyin: Wǒ bǎ dǎcuò de huà chèhuí le, hái yòng wúhén chèhuí shān le tíshì, kě duìmiàn háishi néng kàndào "duìfāng chèhuí le yī tiáo xiāoxi", yīdiǎn yòng dōu méiyǒu.
example_translation: I recalled the message I mistyped and used traceless-recall to delete the notice on my side too, but the other person can still see "the other party recalled a message" — completely useless.
context: WeChat rolled this out in version 8.0.76 (July 2026): long-press the grey "you recalled a message" bubble to delete it from your own chat history. It immediately drew backlash for being one-sided — deleting your own copy does nothing to stop the recipient from seeing the recall notice on their end. Netizens split into two camps: office workers glad to tidy up their own screenshots, and everyone else mocking it as fake "traceless-ness" and demanding a real two-way version. The gap between the feature's name and what it actually does made it an instant target for the chengyu [[yan-er-dao-ling]].

meaning: To deceive only yourself — plugging your own ears while stealing a bell, reasoning that if you can't hear it ring, no one else can either. Used for anyone who hides an obvious problem from themselves while it stays plainly visible to everyone else.
meaning_zh: 比喻自己欺骗自己：明明掩盖不了的事情，却偏要蒙蔽自己的耳目，以为自己看不见、听不见，别人也一样不知道。
example: 你把撤回提示删了，对方照样看得到，这不就是当代版掩耳盗铃吗？
example_pinyin: Nǐ bǎ chèhuí tíshì shān le, duìfāng zhàoyàng kàn de dào, zhè bú jiùshì dāngdài bǎn yǎn ěr dào líng ma?
example_translation: You deleted the recall notice, but the other person can still see it just the same — isn't that basically a modern-day "covering your ears while stealing a bell"?
context: An ancient Warring States-era fable (recorded in the Lüshi Chunqiu) about a thief who covers his own ears while stealing a bell, thinking that since he can't hear it ring, nobody else will either. It's a fixture of netizen commentary for any half-measure that only fools the person doing it — most recently revived in July 2026 to mock WeChat's one-sided [[wuhen-chehui]] feature, since scrubbing the notice from your own screen does nothing to stop the other person from seeing it.

meaning: Describes someone who nods along and agrees with everything, apologises instantly and cheerfully the moment they're called out, but doesn't actually change their behaviour afterward — named for how the AI chatbot Doubao responds when corrected.
meaning_zh: 网络流行语，形容表面顺从、一被指出错误就笑嘻嘻立刻认错道歉，但转头该怎么做还怎么做、其实根本没往心里去的人；因为这种“嘴上服软、行动不变”的模式很像AI助手豆包应对纠错时的语气，所以得名。
example: 他就是典型的豆包型人格，说他错了立马道歉，下次照样迟到。
example_pinyin: Tā jiù shì diǎnxíng de dòubāo xíng réngé, shuō tā cuò le lìmǎ dàoqiàn, xià cì zhàoyàng chídào.
example_translation: He's a classic "Doubao-type personality" — the moment you say he's wrong he apologises, then shows up late again next time.
context: Named after 豆包 (Doubao), ByteDance's AI chatbot, whose conversational style — instantly agreeable, quick to say sorry when corrected, but not really adjusting its underlying behaviour — became a recognisable pattern. Netizens started applying the label to coworkers and friends who "handle" conflict the same way: high emotional-value charm to smooth things over rather than actually engaging with the criticism. It has spread especially in workplace contexts as a semi-affectionate, semi-exasperated description of people who've perfected "attitude good, behaviour unchanged."

meaning: An emphatic way of saying "definitely" or "guaranteed" — used to affirm or promise something with confidence.
meaning_zh: 网络流行语，“包”在这里表示“肯定、保证”的意思，“包的”相当于“那必须的”“肯定啊”，用来斩钉截铁地表达确定或承诺。
example: 明天准时到？包的！
example_pinyin: Míngtiān zhǔnshí dào? Bāo de!
example_translation: Showing up on time tomorrow? Guaranteed!
context: Traces back to a gaming livestreamer nicknamed Coke — when fans jokingly pretended not to recognise him, commenters would reply "包变脸的" ("guaranteed he'll change his tune"), using 包 the way some regional dialects use it to mean "for sure." The shorthand "包的" broke out of that fandom bubble into general use, prized for sounding punchier and more confident than a plain "肯定" or "好的."

meaning: A 2026 overseas TikTok trend where non-Chinese users film themselves adopting Chinese lifestyle habits — drinking hot water, wearing cotton slippers, cooking congee and soup, doing baduanjin exercises — as a half-joking, half-sincere wellness challenge.
meaning_zh: 2026年初在海外社交媒体走红的挑战梗：起初是一位华裔博主分享喝热水、驱寒保暖等养生习惯，半开玩笑地喊网友“从明天开始你要变成中国人了”，随后各国网友争相模仿喝热水、煲汤煮粥、穿棉拖鞋等“中式生活方式”，把它当成健康自律的打卡挑战。
example: 最近好多外国博主都在晒“成为中国人”挑战，天天煮粥喝热水。
example_pinyin: Zuìjìn hǎoduō wàiguó bózhǔ dōu zài shài "chéngwéi Zhōngguórén" tiǎozhàn, tiāntiān zhǔ zhōu hē rèshuǐ.
example_translation: Lately loads of foreign creators have been posting their "becoming Chinese" challenge — cooking congee and drinking hot water every day.
context: Started when a Chinese-American creator posted tips like drinking hot water and avoiding cold food to stay healthy, jokingly telling followers "starting tomorrow, you're becoming Chinese." The video racked up millions of views and spawned a wave of imitators worldwide who began daily check-ins of habits like hot soup, cotton slippers, and red scarves for luck — framed not as mockery but as genuine admiration for what they saw as practical Eastern wellness wisdom, making it 2026's first big cross-border meme out of China.

meaning: A plush toy mascot shaped like a garlic-headed yellow bird that "speaks" Wuhan dialect when squeezed — it says something that sounds like 算了 ("suàn le", meaning "forget it, let it go"). Not a piece of vocabulary with a portable meaning so much as a viral merchandise phenomenon: people buy and gift it as a cute, comforting way of saying "let it go, don't stress."
meaning_zh: 一种大蒜头造型的黄色小鸟毛绒玩具，捏一下会用武汉方言说出类似"算了"的声音。它不是一个有固定含义的词，而是一款爆红的文创玩偶：靠谐音和萌感传递"算了，别往心里去"的安慰感。
example: 别纠结了，买只蒜鸟捏一捏，蒜鸟蒜鸟。
example_pinyin: Bié jiūjié le, mǎi zhī suànniǎo niē yi niē, suàn niǎo suàn niǎo.
example_translation: Stop stressing about it — go squeeze a suan niao, let it go, let it go.
context: Wuhan native Li Mangguo made the first one from a sprouted garlic bulb to cheer up his wife after an argument, riffing on the Wuhan dialect phrase 算了 ("suàn le", let it go) sounding like 蒜鸟 ("suàn niǎo", garlic bird). The garlic-head design nods to the classic garnish on Wuhan hot-dry noodles. It went viral on Douyin and Xiaohongshu through 2025, sold over 100,000 units, spawned sibling dialect plushies, and became a fixture of Wuhan tourist shops and gift shelves — still circulating as a byword for "chill out" going into 2026.

meaning: "Immersion"/"sense of being there" — the feeling of stepping into a video's perspective rather than just watching it, chased through POV framing, first-person narration, and ASMR-style sound design so the viewer feels present in the scene rather than an outside observer.
meaning_zh: 指观众看内容时产生的"身临其境"的感觉，仿佛自己就在画面里，而不只是旁观。常通过第一视角(POV)、第一人称叙述、ASMR式的环境音效来营造。
example: 这条第一视角做饭视频代入感也太强了，看完感觉自己刚吃完饭。
example_pinyin: Zhè tiáo dì-yī shìjiǎo zuò fàn shìpín dàirùgǎn yě tài qiáng le, kàn wán gǎnjué zìjǐ gāng chī wán fàn.
example_translation: This first-person cooking video has such strong immersion, I feel like I just ate after watching it.
context: Named by Xiaohongshu's 2026 "top ten hot words" data report as one of the platform's defining content trends: POV clips, ASMR sound design and first-person narration exploded in popularity because viewers were chasing the feeling of being physically present in a scene rather than watching from outside. Douyin's "immersive" (沉浸式) tag alone has racked up billions of views, and 代入感 became the shorthand critics and creators use for why this style of content performs so well.

meaning: "The strength of softness" — a life philosophy of being outwardly gentle but inwardly resilient: using warmth, patience and emotional flexibility as your source of strength instead of toughness or aggression, and living out your own values quietly rather than by force.
meaning_zh: 一种"外柔内韧"的生活哲学：用温柔、耐心和情绪上的灵活性作为自己的力量来源，而不是靠强硬或对抗；不张扬，却能凭内在智慧活出自己的样子。
example: 她从不跟人硬碰硬，但总能把事情办成，这就是柔软力。
example_pinyin: Tā cóng bù gēn rén yìngpèngyìng, dàn zǒng néng bǎ shìqing bàn chéng, zhè jiù shì róuruǎnlì.
example_translation: She never confronts people head-on, but she always gets things done — that's 柔软力 (the strength of softness).
context: One of Xiaohongshu's 2026 "top ten hot words", surfacing alongside 活人感 and 边界感 as part of a broader shift toward self-care and interiority: users increasingly frame emotional gentleness — being soft rather than combative — as a deliberate strength rather than a weakness, in contrast to older "hustle culture" ideals of toughness and grinding through.

meaning: Shorthand for 'the grind you can't quite escape' — an unglamorous hometown, job, or daily routine that wears you down, even though it once held warmth too. People say 我想离开浪浪山 ('I want to leave Langlang Mountain') to voice the urge to get out of a rut without necessarily knowing where to go instead.
meaning_zh: 网络流行语，指那个磨人却难以真正离开的'家乡'或日常处境——也许不够发达甚至有些贫瘠，却承载过温暖的记忆。打工人常用'我想离开浪浪山'表达想逃离现状（工作、家乡、生活）的心情，即便不知道能去哪。
example: 每天加班到十点，我真的很想离开浪浪山。

example_translation: Working overtime until 10pm every day, I really just want to escape this grind.
context: From the 2023 animated short 《小妖怪的夏天》 (part of the anthology series 中国奇谭), where a small pig-demon toils under an exploitative demon boss in a place called 浪浪山, dreaming of leaving. meaning: Beijing slang for someone who's being loud, showy, or over-the-top — can land as a compliment, a playful tease, or genuine exasperation depending on tone. Roughly 'you're being wild as hell' or 'you're really putting on a show, huh'.
meaning_zh: 带有老北京方言味儿的调侃用语，形容某人嚣张、高调、爱显摆或行为夸张。语气可以是夸奖、玩笑式吐槽，也可以是真的看不下去了，全看场合和语气。

Short-video creators paired the two into 丫够燥的 in reaction videos and comment sections, and it caught on nationwide in the first half of 2026 as an all-purpose reaction to anyone being extra.

meaning: A viral self-soothing trick: instead of sighing downward with your head bowed and shoulders slumped (which signals 'I give up'), tilt your head back, open your chest, and exhale skyward — supposedly resetting your mood instead of reinforcing it. People film themselves doing it, often set to music.
meaning_zh: 近期爆火的解压小技巧：不再是低头弓背地向下叹气（传递'我不行了'的信号），而是抬头挺胸、望着天空把气叹出去，据说这样能让大脑收到'我在释放、我要重启'的信号，而不是加重emo。许多人拍视频记录自己'向上叹气'，还常配上音乐。
example: 心情不好的时候别老低头叹气，试试向上叹气，据说真的有用。
example_pinyin: Xīnqíng bù hǎo de shíhou bié lǎo dītóu tànqì, shìshì xiàng shàng tànqì, jùshuō zhēn de yǒuyòng.
example_translation: When you're feeling down, don't just sigh with your head bowed — try sighing upward instead, apparently it actually works.
context: The technique traces to psychology's 'facial feedback hypothesis' — that posture and breathing can shape emotion rather than just express it. It spread from a livestreamer demonstrating it in May 2026, got a boost when a celebrity posted about it in June, and exploded in July as short-video creators set their upward sighs to sentimental pop songs, turning a breathing tip into a full-blown decompression meme.

meaning_zh: 一段刻意荒诞、洗脑的说唱即兴哼唱爆红成为全网热梗，歌词反复唱'中国人能飞，黄皮肤才对，讲中文才飞，中国就是美'。表面无厘头，但网友们既读出了民族自豪感（卫星、飞船、空间站、大飞机都能'飞'上天），也当作一句万能的自我打气口号来玩梗。

meaning: A viral 'choice → praise' template that began with a house cat being shown a carrot and a tissue and asked to pick, then getting cooed at with '真棒!' (so good!) no matter what it chose. meaning: A classical fable-turned-idiom for someone who rigidly applies an old rule to a changed situation — like the man who dropped his sword overboard, carved a notch on the boat to mark the spot, and later dove in at the notch even though the boat (and the sword) had long since moved. Used online to call out anyone — a policy, a boss, a strategy — that refuses to adapt when circumstances have shifted.
meaning_zh: 出自《吕氏春秋》的寓言：楚人剑掉入江中，在船舷刻记号，船靠岸后却按刻痕处下水找剑——殊不知船已经移动，剑早不在原处了。现多用来批评那些不知变通、死守旧规矩、忽视客观情况已经改变的人或做法。
example: 都什么年代了还用老办法管新团队，这不是刻舟求剑吗？
example_pinyin: Dōu shénme niándài le hái yòng lǎo bànfǎ guǎn xīn tuánduì, zhè bù shì kè zhōu qiú jiàn ma?
example_translation: It's a different era now and you're still managing the new team with old methods — isn't that just marking the boat to find the sword?
context: One of the oldest fables in the Chinese school curriculum (from 《吕氏春秋·察今》), but it stays alive in comment sections precisely because it's such a compact put-down: people reach for it whenever someone applies an outdated rulebook — a manager's playbook, an investor's old thesis, a parent's fixed idea of 'how things are done' — to a situation that has since changed underneath them.

hanzi: 一代人有一代人的僵尸肉
pinyin: yí dài rén yǒu yí dài rén de jiāngshī ròu
literal: one generation + has + one generation's + zombie meat
meaning: A wry generational joke about freezer-hoarding: every generation has its own 'zombie meat' — food frozen so long it's practically undead — whether that's a parent's decades-old cured pork wrapped like a brick, or a younger person's forgotten oat milk and meal-prep containers. Used to point out that hoarding habits just take different forms across generations, not that any generation is exempt.
meaning_zh: 网络热梗，调侃两代人冰箱里都藏着'僵尸肉'——冻了太久、几乎'成精'的食物。老一辈可能是腌成砖头一样的腊肉、放了几年的排骨；年轻一代则是囤积却忘记喝的燕麦奶、吃了一半的预制菜。意思是'断舍离'这件事人人都懂但人人都做不到，只是每代人囤积的东西不一样。
example: 别笑我妈的腊肉了，你冰箱里那盒过期酸奶不也是你这代人的僵尸肉。
example_pinyin: Bié xiào wǒ mā de làròu le, nǐ bīngxiāng lǐ nà hé guòqī suānnǎi bù yě shì nǐ zhè dài rén de jiāngshī ròu.
example_translation: Don't laugh at my mum's cured pork — that expired yogurt in your fridge is your generation's zombie meat too.
context: The phrase surfaced in July 2026 alongside a wave of social posts and news pieces comparing what different generations let go bad in their freezers — a parent's meat frozen for years next to a twenty-something's abandoned oat milk and takeout leftovers. It works as gentle intergenerational ribbing rather than real criticism: the joke isn't that older people hoard and younger people don't, it's that everyone has a version of the same habit.

meaning: A catchphrase for shutting down a topic without explaining or justifying yourself — roughly 'not gonna get into it' or 'say no more'. Used to imitate a fiercely partial, doesn't-care-about-fairness attitude, most often self-deprecatingly or to describe someone playing favourites.
meaning_zh: 网络流行语，意思接近'不解释了、不想说了、别的都不重要'，常带点护短、偏心、不讲道理的意味。多用来自嘲或调侃某人一味偏袒某个对象、别的什么都不管不顾。

example_translation: As long as my cat is happy, I don't care that the furniture's wrecked — not gonna get into it.

The line caught on as shorthand for blind favouritism or refusing to justify a biased decision, applied well beyond the original grandma-and-grandson context.

meaning: To blindly copy someone else's style or success without understanding what actually made it work, ending up looking worse than before you tried. From the Zhuangzi parable: the plain-looking Dongshi saw that the famous beauty Xishi looked charming even while clutching her chest and frowning in pain, so she copied the frown herself — only to look ridiculous rather than beautiful.
meaning_zh: 比喻盲目模仿别人，却不明白对方好看/成功的真正原因，结果适得其反、更加丑陋可笑。出自《庄子》寓言：丑女东施看到美女西施因病捂胸皱眉的样子很动人，便刻意模仿，结果反而吓跑了邻里。
example: 别人减肥成功是靠控制饮食，你天天喝代餐粉却照吃夜宵，真是东施效颦。
example_pinyin: Biérén jiǎnféi chénggōng shì kào kòngzhì yǐnshí, nǐ tiāntiān hē dàicānfěn què zhào chī yèxiāo, zhēnshi dōngshī xiàopín.
example_translation: Other people lost weight by actually controlling their diet — you drink meal-replacement powder but still eat late-night snacks; that's just a clumsy copy that misses the point.
context: A classical chengyu that never left everyday use, and it's especially alive in comment sections today: netizens reach for it whenever a brand, influencer, or celebrity copies a viral trend (a dance, a marketing stunt, a rival's look) without grasping why the original worked, and the copy flops or looks awkward instead.

meaning_zh: 把"打工人"（2020年爆红的打工人自嘲梗）和"人传人"（医学术语，指疾病人传人）拼在一起的调侃说法，形容"打工人"这个称呼和"早安打工人"之类的语录像病毒一样在各行各业迅速蔓延、人人跟风自称"打工人"的现象。

example_translation: From construction sites to office towers, this wave of 'morning, fellow worker' really has spread person-to-person — nobody's immune.

meaning: A stock phrase workers post to a group chat or boss the moment they sit down: 'At my desk, replying instantly.' It signals 'I'm on the clock and reachable' — sometimes sincerely, sometimes as deadpan self-mockery for being tethered to messaging apps the second you arrive.
meaning_zh: 打工人一到工位就发的一句话，意思是"我已经到岗，随时秒回消息"。既可以是真心汇报自己进入工作状态，也可以是自嘲——调侃自己一坐下就要被工作消息"绑架"，摸鱼都不敢明目张胆。
example: 老板一早发消息，我立刻回了句'已到工位秒回'，其实心里在想今天摸鱼摸到几点。

example_translation: The boss messaged first thing, and I instantly replied 'at my desk, replying instantly' — though secretly I was wondering how long I could slack off today.
context: A 2026 workplace catchphrase that's part genuine status update, part inside joke: typing it out the second you arrive doubles as proof of diligence for managers and as dark humour among coworkers, who use it to describe being permanently on-call from the moment they cross the office threshold — even while quietly 摸鱼 (slacking off) between messages.

meaning: A mad-libs template phrase — "[X] basic, [Y] not basic" — used to point out a jarring, funny contrast between two things that are supposed to match (e.g. a plain top with a wild bottom, a modest salary with wild spending). Expanded from a fashion tip into an all-purpose "unexpectedly extra" joke format.
meaning_zh: 一种句式流行语，格式为"XX基础，XX不基础"，用来调侃两件本该匹配的事物之间出人意料的反差和不协调，比如"上衣基础，下装不基础"。后来被网友套用到生活各领域，表达"意料之外的离谱反差"。
example: 别看他工资基础，消费可一点不基础。
example_pinyin: Bié kàn tā gōngzī jīchǔ, xiāofèi kě yìdiǎn bù jīchǔ.
example_translation: Don't be fooled by his modest salary — his spending is anything but modest.
context: Originated from a fashion blogger's styling tip: "上身基础，下身就不基础" (basic top, not-basic bottom) — pairing a plain blazer with wild, colour-clashing pieces below for contrast. Netizens loved the mismatched-but-it-works effect and started applying the "X basic, Y not basic" template everywhere — salary vs spending, a calm mind vs an insane exam question, and so on. It was named one of 2025's top ten internet buzzwords.

meaning: A mock-serious catchphrase used when something someone said or did is so profound, absurd, or relatable that the only fitting response is joking about quitting your job to devote your life to studying it. Netizens slot in whatever sparked the reaction after 研究 ("study").
meaning_zh: 网络热梗句式，字面是"我要辞职回家专门研究这段话/这件事"，用来夸张地表达某句话或某件事让人深受触动、觉得意味深长，值得反复回味、深入研究。常用于评论区玩梗跟风。
example: 他这段话说得太通透了，我将辞职在家研究他。

example_translation: What he said was so enlightened, I'm going to quit my job and study him full-time.

Netizens turned his sincerity into self-deprecating comedy: "我将辞职在家研究苏醒" (I'll quit my job to study Su Xing) went viral, and the template spread to any statement or person netizens find weirdly profound or funny.

Paired with "爆了" for extra punch, it broke out via a cartoon character's catchphrase online and then exploded when the 2026 Spring Festival Gala and official state media started using it too, cementing it as the year's go-to compliment.

meaning_zh: 指被工作压榨、像牲口一样被使唤的打工人，多用于自嘲或吐槽职场剥削，语气比“打工人”更愤懑、更强调被压榨感。
example: 加班到十一点，我真的是纯纯的城市牛马。

example_translation: Working overtime until 11pm, I really am just a pure city ox-and-horse.

It stuck as shorthand for anyone slogging through exploitative work, and by 2026 has largely eclipsed the older, gentler “打工人” as the go-to word for describing overwork, precisely because it carries more bitterness about being used up for someone else's benefit.

meaning: A sarcastic comment-section stock phrase: pretending to be outraged that someone withheld some "crucial" piece of information, when the information is actually completely obvious or irrelevant. Used to needle low-effort or redundant comments.
meaning_zh: 评论区常用的反讽公式梗，字面是“这么重要的事你怎么不早说”，实际是调侃对方说了句废话或人尽皆知的信息，带着一种配合演出的幽默感。

Screenshotted and passed around, it became the standard reply netizens now paste under obvious or filler comments — a way of "playing along" with a joke rather than genuinely complaining.

meaning: A viral 2026 meme: a photo of a real opossum caught standing upright indoors, hands folded behind its back, staring blankly out a window. Netizens — especially office workers (打工人) — adopted it as a mascot because an opossum's signature defence is to freeze and 'play dead' rather than flee, which mirrors how it feels to face deadlines and bosses: outwardly composed, inwardly already checked out.
meaning_zh: 2026年爆红的表情包，源自一张海外网友抓拍的照片：一只负鼠溜进屋内，被发现后背手站立、呆望窗外。因为负鼠天性是遇到危险就'装死'僵住而不是逃跑，打工人借此自嘲面对工作、消息和老板时'精神已经进入负鼠模式'——表面淡定，内心早已放弃思考。
example: 老板又在群里@我了，我已经进入负鼠模式了。
example_pinyin: Lǎobǎn yòu zài qún lǐ @ wǒ le, wǒ yǐjīng jìnrù fùshǔ móshì le.
example_translation: The boss @-mentioned me in the group chat again — I've already switched to possum mode.
context: Originated from a candid overseas photo of an opossum that snuck indoors and froze upright, hands folded, staring out a window when discovered. Chinese netizens personified it around the English phrase 'play possum' — an animal whose entire survival strategy is pretending to be dead when threatened. It exploded on Xiaohongshu (80M+ views) and Bilibili from mid-2026 onward as the perfect stand-in for 打工人 exhaustion: you can't literally collapse at your desk, but spiritually you already have.

meaning: A 2026 workplace self-deprecating label for someone stuck at the '45-degree angle' between 0° (full 躺平/lying flat) and 90° (full 内卷/grinding) — too worn out to hustle hard, too anxious about rent and ageing parents to fully give up.
meaning_zh: 2026年职场自嘲词，用几何角度打比方：0°是完全躺平，90°是拼命内卷，'夹角打工人'就是卡在中间的45°——卷不动也躺不平，被'不卷就被淘汰'和'及时行乐'两种声音反复拉扯。
example: 别问我卷不卷，我就是个夹角打工人，卡在中间动不了。
example_pinyin: Bié wèn wǒ juǎn bu juǎn, wǒ jiùshì ge jiājiǎo dǎgōngrén, kǎ zài zhōngjiān dòng bu liǎo.
example_translation: Don't ask me whether I'm grinding or not — I'm a 45-degree worker, stuck in the middle and unable to move either way.
context: Coined collectively by workplace-venting bloggers on Douyin, Xiaohongshu and Weibo around May 2026, with no single viral source video. It reframes the older 内卷 (grinding) vs 躺平 (lying flat) binary as a geometry joke: most workers aren't fully at either extreme, they're stuck at the 'included angle' in between, torn between doom-scrolling 'if you don't hustle you'll be replaced' content and 'seize the day' content, while real constraints — mortgages, ageing parents, stalled careers — keep them from moving either way. It marks a shift from earlier, simpler 打工人 (worker) self-pity memes toward naming the structural bind itself.

meaning: Chinese nickname for American livestreamer iShowSpeed (Darren Watkins Jr.), coined because his manic, exaggerated on-camera reactions resemble the hyperactivity of hyperthyroid disease. Now also used more generally to tease anyone acting wildly over-the-top in front of a camera.
meaning_zh: 中国网友给美国主播iShowSpeed（达伦·沃特金斯）起的外号，因为他直播时夸张亢奋的反应像甲状腺功能亢进（甲亢）发作；现在也被用来调侃任何在镜头前情绪特别激动、上蹿下跳的人。
example: 他一看到自己抽到SSR就开始满屋子跑，跟甲亢哥附体一样。
example_pinyin: Tā yí kàndào zìjǐ chōudào SSR jiù kāishǐ mǎn wū pǎo, gēn Jiǎkàng Gē fùtǐ yíyàng.
example_translation: The moment he pulled an SSR he started running around the room like he'd been possessed by Jiǎkàng Gē.
context: 外号源自2022年他反应大张伟《阳光彩虹小白马》的视频，因表情肢体太夸张、像甲亢发作而被中国网友起了这个名字。2025年4月他来华直播中国行后彻底破圈，2026年世界杯期间又和"退钱哥"互动喊话，8月还因直播中手机掉进海里被中国网友玩梗刷屏。

meaning: Nickname for Chinese football fan He Sheng, caught on a live TV mic in 2016 shouting "Refund!" at reporters after the men's national team lost to Syria. Now used as a stock reaction for furious, disappointed fans who feel they deserve their money back.
meaning_zh: 中国球迷何胜的外号。2016年国足客场0比1负于叙利亚后，他在直播镜头前对记者喊出"对得起我们吗？退钱！"，瞬间走红；现在常被用来调侃任何觉得自己"看了场寂寞"、想讨回票钱的失望观众。
example: 这场比赛踢得也太拉了，我都想学退钱哥喊一句"退钱"了。
example_pinyin: Zhè chǎng bǐsài tī de yě tài lā le, wǒ dōu xiǎng xué Tuìqián Gē hǎn yī jù "tuì qián" le.
example_translation: This match was so bad I wanted to channel Refund Bro and yell "Refund!"
context: 2016年十强赛国足客场负于叙利亚后，何胜的直播喊话被记者话筒直接收音、来不及切镜头，视频瞬间传遍全网。2026年美加墨世界杯期间，他自费到现场为国足助威，还与美国主播"甲亢哥"直播互动学"退钱"梗，让这个老梗又火了一轮。

meaning: A joke about how manic Chinese university back-to-school weeks have become — nonstop reunion dinners, hotpot, BBQ, milk tea runs and club-recruitment treats — so packed with eating that it looks less like term starting and more like a wedding banquet.
meaning_zh: 调侃现在大学开学场面太热闹，新生报到、老同学重逢、社团招新全变成了聚餐局，火锅、烧烤、日料、奶茶轮番上阵，热闹得分不清到底是开学还是办酒席。
example: 我们宿舍这两天天天有饭局，真是应了那句"开学即开席"。
example_pinyin: Wǒmen sùshè zhè liǎng tiān tiāntiān yǒu fànjú, zhēnshi yìngle nà jù "kāixué jí kāixí".
example_translation: Our dorm's had a group dinner every single day this week — living proof that "term starting is basically a banquet starting."
context: 2026年9月开学季，微博话题#这到底是开学还是开席#火了，网友晒出各校迎新现场：锣鼓横幅、摊位福利、聚餐接龙，调侃大学新生"第一天约饭，第二天吃席，第三天已经找不到空闲的肚子了"。

meaning: A joking phrase for when an AI service like ChatGPT goes down or glitches en masse — especially funny when it happens right as the company is busy hyping how powerful the model is.
meaning_zh: 调侃ChatGPT等AI服务突然大面积宕机、卡顿或报错的说法，常用在厂商刚吹完模型多强、结果服务反而先崩了的场合，形成反差笑点。
example: 官方刚宣布进入AGI时代，结果GPT炸了，网友：这就是传说中的AGI（艰难）时代吧。
example_pinyin: Guānfāng gāng xuānbù jìnrù AGI shídài, jiéguǒ GPT zhà le, wǎngyǒu: zhè jiùshì chuánshuō zhōng de AGI (jiānnán) shídài ba.
example_translation: They'd just announced we'd entered the AGI era, and then GPT crashed — netizens joked, "guess this is the legendary Age of Great Inconvenience."
context: 2026年9月3日OpenAI发布GPT-6（"Astra"），总裁Greg Brockman宣称"我们可能已经实现AGI"；当晚ChatGPT、Claude、Grok等却同时出现大面积异常，中文AI社区网友纷纷刷"GPT炸了""我的GPT要挺住啊"，调侃AGI宣言和服务器崩溃同时发生的反差。

literal: steamed clam (a mishearing of 真棒 "really great")
meaning: A homophone-mishearing meme: netizens misheard "真棒" (zhēn bàng, "awesome!") as "蒸蚌" (zhēng bàng, "steamed clam") in a viral cat video, and now use 蒸蚌 itself as a goofy, endearing way to say "amazing!"
meaning_zh: "蒸蚌"是"真棒"的空耳谐音梗，源自一只靠瞎蒙讨主人欢心的猫。网友现在直接用"蒸蚌"代替"真棒"来夸奖，带一种憨萌荒诞的语气。
example: 你这波操作蒸蚌！
example_pinyin: Nǐ zhè bō cāozuò zhēng bàng!
example_translation: That move of yours is amazing!
context: Originates from Douyin pet blogger 超级无敌大开门's cat-training videos: she lays out items like a carrot and a tissue and asks her three-coloured cat "大开门" to touch the right one, rewarding a correct guess with an enthusiastic "真棒!" (zhēn bàng). When the clips spread to Weibo, commenters joked they misheard "真棒" as "蒸蚌" (steamed clam) over the cat's confused face, and the nonsense phrase itself went viral at the end of 2025 as the "萝卜纸巾猫" (carrot-tissue cat) meme — even celebrities like Zhou Shen (周深) picked up the pun.

meaning: Borrowed from zoo husbandry (environmental enrichment for captive animals — giving them stimulation so they don't develop stereotypic behaviours from boredom). Young people now use it self-deprecatingly to mean actively enriching their own dull, repetitive routine — a walk, a hobby, a treat — as a way of fighting burnout, as if giving themselves the same care a zookeeper gives a caged animal.
meaning_zh: 原是动物园饲养学术语，指通过增加刺激和环境变化，让圈养动物表现自然行为、改善身心状态，防止出现刻板行为。年轻人借用这个词自嘲地形容给自己单调重复的生活“加料”——找点新鲜事、小乐趣，对抗班味和精神内耗，就像饲养员给动物做丰容一样。
example: 周末去公园遛了一圈，给自己丰容一下，不然真要班味上脑了。
example_pinyin: Zhōumò qù gōngyuán liù le yī quān, gěi zìjǐ fēngróng yīxià, bùrán zhēn yào bānwèi shàngnǎo le.
example_translation: I took a walk in the park this weekend to enrich myself a bit — otherwise the office funk was really going to my head.
context: 丰容 ("enrichment") is a 1998 zoo-husbandry concept for stimulating captive animals so they don't develop boredom-driven stereotypic behaviour. It surfaced on Xiaohongshu's 2026 "top ten words" list after young office workers started applying it to themselves — comparing their own repetitive 996 routines to a zoo enclosure, and using 丰容 as shorthand for deliberately building novelty and self-care into their week.

meaning: A good-luck exclamation — "may fortune come!" — that exploded via the 2024 viral rap song 《八方来财》("Fortune from all directions") by Cantonese rapper 揽佬. People now chant or type it before an exam, interview, or gacha pull for luck, and it spawned a template "来X" (来offer, 来分, i.e. "may the offer/grade come").
meaning_zh: 源自说唱歌手“揽佬”2024年的洗脑神曲《八方来财》，歌词朗朗上口，网友把它当祈福口头禅——考试前、面试前、抽卡前喊一句“来财”，图个好运，后来衍生出“来offer”“来分”等万能句式。2025年入选年度十大网络流行语。
example: 明天面试，来财来财，祝我上岸！
example_pinyin: Míngtiān miànshì, lái cái lái cái, zhù wǒ shàng'àn!
example_translation: Interview tomorrow — come fortune, come fortune, wish me luck landing it!
context: 《八方来财》 was released by rapper 揽佬 in August 2024, blending Cantonese folk motifs with Memphis rap and lyrics mocking people who beg the gods for money while cutting corners. It went viral in early 2025, racking up over 10 billion plays and getting sung by grandparents and toddlers alike; by December 2025 the state-run language monitoring centre had named 来财 one of the year's ten defining slang terms.

literal: old man + toy with/tease + naughty + child
meaning: Describes a veteran or expert effortlessly toying with a far weaker opponent in a game, match, or esports round — a vivider, more mock-classical replacement for the older, blunter gaming slang "炸鱼" (netting fish, i.e. stomping newbies). Used self-deprecatingly by the loser or admiringly by onlookers.
meaning_zh: 形容高手对新手形成碾压级的实力差距，轻松愉快地“戏耍”对手，多见于游戏、棋类、电竞解说和体育比赛场景，是“炸鱼”一词更生动、更有画面感的新说法，带调侃意味。
example: 这局大神带我这个萌新，纯纯老叟戏顽童。
example_pinyin: Zhè jú dàshén dài wǒ zhège méngxīn, chúnchún lǎosǒu xì wántóng.
example_translation: That pro carried me, a total noob, this round — a pure case of the old man toying with the kid.
context: The phrase spread through gaming and esports communities across titles (黑神话：悟空, tank/MOBA matches, Go-themed anime clips) in 2026 as a wittier stand-in for "炸鱼", with Bilibili explainer videos ("梗百科") and a Baidu Baike entry cementing it as this year's go-to term for a lopsided stomp.

meaning: "Digital hoarding syndrome" — compulsively bookmarking, favouriting, or downloading articles, tutorials, and games and never actually opening them, like a hamster stuffing its cheeks with food it never eats. Often driven by FOMO and the illusion that "saved = learned".
meaning_zh: 形容像仓鼠囤粮一样疯狂收藏文章、教程、游戏等数字内容却从不打开、不消费的行为——“收藏即学会”的错觉，本质是一种数字囤积症，常源于错失恐惧症（FOMO）。
example: 我收藏夹里三千篇干货一篇没看完，典型电子仓鼠症晚期。
example_pinyin: Wǒ shōucángjiā lǐ sānqiān piān gānhuò yī piān méi kàn wán, diǎnxíng diànzǐ cāngshǔzhèng wǎnqī.
example_translation: I've got three thousand "must-read" articles saved and haven't finished a single one — textbook late-stage digital hoarding syndrome.
context: Grew out of years of "数字囤积/电子囤积症" (digital hoarding) discourse — Steam gamers' "喜加一" habit of grabbing every free game and never playing it is often cited as a sub-case — and crystallised recently into the punchier "电子仓鼠(症)" label, now a stock self-deprecating tag for anyone whose bookmarks folder outpaces their reading.

meaning: Being physically at your desk but mentally checked out — doing the bare minimum because your mind has already "clocked off", even though your body is still at work. An extension of the older 摸鱼 (fish-slacking) idea, but about mental disengagement rather than sneaking in side activities.
meaning_zh: 指人身体还在工位上，但精神已经"下班"了，只完成最低限度的工作量。是"摸鱼"概念在心理层面的延伸，强调的是内心的抽离而非偷偷摸鱼。
example: 开完那个没完没了的会，我整个人精神下班了，剩下的工作全靠惯性。
example_pinyin: Kāiwán nà ge méiwánméiliǎo de huì, wǒ zhěnggè rén jīngshén xiàbān le, shèngxià de gōngzuò quán kào guànxìng.
example_translation: After that endless meeting I mentally clocked out — the rest of my work is just running on autopilot.
context: One of Digitaling's top 30 internet buzzwords for H1 2026. It captures a burnout-adjacent mood among office workers who no longer bother hiding their disengagement — a step beyond 摸鱼 (covert slacking) into open, low-effort presenteeism.

meaning: "Hold it together" — telling yourself (or someone else) to keep a straight face and not crack up laughing or break down crying, in the face of something absurd, cringe, or overwhelming.
meaning_zh: 形容在离谱、搞笑或令人崩溃的场面前，努力忍住不笑或不崩溃。是老梗"蚌埠住了"（绷不住了）的反向用法——从"绷不住"变成一句要绷住的自我提醒。
example: 他一本正经地念错了自己的名字，我们全场绷住没笑出声。
example_pinyin: Tā yī běnzhèngjīng de niàn cuò le zìjǐ de míngzi, wǒmen quánchǎng bēngzhù méi xiào chū shēng.
example_translation: He solemnly mispronounced his own name, and somehow the whole room held it together without laughing.
context: A 2026 offshoot of the older pun "蚌埠住了" (Bengbu city + 绷不住了 "can't hold it together"), which broke out of 抗压背锅吧-style forums and 二创 comment sections around 2020. "绷住" flips the collapsed version back into an imperative, and has spawned its own mini-vocabulary: 难绷 (hard to hold it together), 老绷家 (a chronic can't-keep-a-straight-face type), 轻松绷住 (holding it together with ease).
